text: The Casimir element $C \in Z(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}))$ acts on the irreducible module $L(\lambda)$ as the scalar:
explanation: The chapter gives the Casimir eigenvalue on $L(\lambda)$ as $(\lambda, \lambda+2\rho)$. Since $(\lambda,\lambda+2\rho) = (\lambda+\rho,\lambda+\rho) - (\rho,\rho)$, the choices $(\lambda+\rho,\lambda+\rho)$ and $(\rho,\rho)$ differ from the answer by the constant $(\rho,\rho)$, while $(\lambda,\lambda)$ drops the $2\rho$ shift entirely.
